Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

weft (development version)

  • chunk_claims: collect now covers Python claim() and Julia @claim. In a knitr document a failed guest claim is recorded under its chunk’s label, returns its value, and the chunk goes on; the render fails at the end with every failure listed. On the Jupyter and julia engines the guest package reads the setting from the document’s front matter and the nearest _weft.yml, displays the failed claim’s block, and goes on, and the filter reports it as before. A Python or Julia chunk error after a collected claim in a knitr document is now reported with the claims listed first, as for R. Under stop (the default) nothing changes. A bad chunk_claims value in a document on the Jupyter or julia engine is now reported as an error. A collected claim in a hidden cell on the engines is lost, a daemon kernel may read a stale front matter (set the key in _weft.yml), and the julia engine and Jupyter engine add no note for a later error.
  • The ledger now records the tables of a document on the Jupyter or Julia engine, and of Markdown run through the filter. The filter writes one table entry for each Pandoc table or HTML table in a cell, keyed by the cell’s label, with a digest of the cells’ text, so changes() reports “table tbl-sites changed” there as it does for R. A table that a script fills in after the page loads is recorded by the HTML it holds, pandas in PDF output prints text and records nothing, and knitr documents are unchanged. These digests do not compare with the R route’s. The first render after you upgrade lists each such table as added, once.
  • The hint for a name published nowhere no longer says “above”: it now reads “Publish it in code in this document”, since a named value may be published below its use.
  • The claim-word lint is quieter. The shipped list drops each, both, either and whole (65 words), skips idioms such as “at least” and “no longer” (claim_words: {idioms: [...]} adds your own), and skips a word with a hyphen beside it or a capital that does not start its sentence. A quantifier is now listed only in a sentence with a value or a digit; the new setting claim_quantifiers (number, any or none) changes that.
  • A claim-word finding in a blockquote no longer shows the > markers, and the last sentence of a list item no longer runs on into the next item’s marker.
  • fmt_num() and fmt_pct() no longer round a number of exactly 15 significant digits one digit early when it lies just below a power of ten: fmt_pct(999999999999999) prints “99,999,999,999,999,900%”, not “100,000,000,000,000,000%”. The Lua filter prints the same.
  • .sci prints a mantissa that rounds up to 10 as an exact 1, so 999000 prints “1 x 106”, as 1e6 does, not “1.0 x 106”. Zero prints as “0” with no exponent.
  • The gate no longer counts a claim() in an R chunk set to eval: false, as it never counted one in a Python or Julia chunk. Turning eval off on a chunk that holds a claim is now a removal.

weft 0.1.0

First release.

Values in prose

  • Inline R with an attribute block prints a computed value through a formatter class: numbers, percentages, p-values, scientific notation, dates, spelled and ordinal counts, lists, ranges and pairs, with keys for decimals, significant figures and list joins. .plus signs a difference; .p takes digits and label.
  • Every class has a function form (fmt_num(), fmt_pct(), fmt_p() and the rest), and weft_str() resolves weft markup in a string from R code.
  • Quantities with units (u()), printed by symbol or name and converted on request.
  • Project settings in _weft.yml for the house style, and project formatters for rules no class covers.

Wording and claims

  • Spans whose wording depends on a value: counts (n), lists (list), conditions and guards (if), and direction (sign), with agreement through ids and back-references.
  • claim() checks a value where it is used and fails the render with the sentence quoted. level = "warn" lists a check without failing. chunk_claims: collect collects failures in chunk code and fails the render at the end.
  • Phrase functions: of_n(), about(), ci() (with short, percentage and signed forms), pm(), clamp(), lookup(), brk() and in_range().
  • arms() lists every wording a document can produce; rehearse() knits it under several sets of parameters.

The dictionary

  • dict.yml holds a project’s chosen values (numbers, quantities, ranges, years, dates, strings, label maps and breaks), each with a definition and an optional decision pointer that verify() resolves. Decision pointers also go on literals, cite spans and claims.
  • A glossary, a Vale rule for spellings to avoid, and dict_seed() to find values that belong in the dictionary.
  • tar_dict() and tar_dict_deps() for targets pipelines.

Other languages and named values

  • Python and Julia values reach prose in knitr documents through py$ and jl_value(), read exactly or refused.
  • Named values: `depth`{.num} in a document on any engine, published from R (weft_put(), weft_values_write()), Python (put(), auto()) or Julia (@put) and resolved by a Pandoc filter. A name can be used above the code that publishes it when it takes one value.

Checking a project

  • lints() reads documents without running them and reports typed numbers, construct errors, cross-reference and citation problems and more.
  • Each render checks its output for unresolved references, values printed as missing and leftover markup, in every format.
  • Each render writes a ledger of the values, wording and tables it printed, and a log of the conditions it raised; changes() compares them with a commit.
  • A commit gate refuses new typed numbers and construct errors, and asks for a trailer when computed values are removed. checks() lists the checks of a project by the value they check.
  • verify() runs the lints, resolves decision pointers, renders every document and checks that no ledger is stale.

Setting up

  • use_weft() sets a project up in one call: activation, Quarto extension and scripts, dictionary, commit hook, GitHub Actions workflow and instructions for coding agents. status() reports what is in place.
